long_biography.plain_text:
Saudi businessman Ghaith Pharaon spent part of his childhood in Paris while his father, Rashad, served as a Saudi ambassador. A physician who became close to the kingdom's founder, his father gave the family influential connections. Pharaon also attended schools in Lebanon, Syria and Switzerland. His contacts included Kamal Adham, who introduced him to BCCI founder Agha Hasan Abedi.

His American bank acquisitions later brought lasting regulatory consequences. In 1997, the Federal Reserve imposed a $37 million civil penalty and permanently barred him from U.S. banking after finding that he had secretly acted for BCCI in buying Independence Bank of Encino. The decision followed an administrative hearing in which his lawyers participated; it was separate from the unresolved criminal charges against him.
